record.title: Phosphazene-Containing Epoxy Resins Based on Bisphenol F with Enhanced Heat Resistance and Mechanical Properties: Synthesis and Properties
claim_notes: Tarasov, Oboishchikova, Borisov, Kireev and Sirotin, Polymers 2022, 14, 4547, published 27 October 2022. Copyright 2022 by the authors; licensee MDPI, Basel, Switzerland.
The article-specific copyright notice on PDF p.1 identifies Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Retain attribution, DOI and license link; no author or publisher endorsement is implied.

Changes: selected nominal feed labels and five measured tensile-strength values transcribed into structured, source-qualified records, with original curation of conditions, explicit unknowns and unresolved source discrepancies. English fallback names are used in all four locale slots.

No separate third-party credit was identified in the inspected Table 1/Table 7 captions or selected synthesis, curing and tensile-method passages. Referenced works, standards text, figures and additional tables are not imported.
The mixed phosphazene-containing epoxy thermosets are treated as source-qualified polymer formulations. No reinforced-composite, pure-species or analytically verified final-composition claim is made.
Selected publisher PDF SHA-256: 1f06bc0667c7c5575a0e88772868a95cd27ba01a264d3b3a0b9c859a8a6423aa. No PDF, screenshots, full text, full tables or raw measurements are redistributed.

provenance.method: Selected publisher-PDF facts and article-specific license notice checked against retained bytes and rendered pages, with separate transcription checks. Finite catalog identity review is software and curation comparison, not independent scientific review, experimental replication or legal clearance.

product_form.text: Cured binder tensile specimens milled from a 4 mm-thick plate.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6, section 2.5.1

product_form.notes: The 4 mm value is source plate thickness, not a measured thickness for every specimen; no reinforcement or generic bulk-property equivalence is inferred.

processing.text: Selected PNA-BPF-1 through PNA-BPF-5 follow the source-described batch addition of solid alkali. DDS hardener was added in a calculated stoichiometric amount; the composition was stirred and degassed on an oil-bath rotor at 125 deg C under a vacuum of 100 mm Hg for 20-40 min until homogeneous, before casting.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.4-5, section 2.2.1; p.5, section 2.4

processing.notes: The KOH/NaOH contradiction remains unresolved. No exact DDS mass fraction, fully specified recipe, conversion or independently verified stoichiometry is assigned.

temper_or_heat_treatment.text: Cured at 180 deg C for 8 h.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5, section 2.4

temper_or_heat_treatment.notes: Cure temperature and duration qualify the state; they are not tensile-test temperature or evidence of complete conversion.

conditioning.notes: Post-cure tensile-specific storage, humidity, moisture and conditioning duration are not reported in the inspected passages.

reinforcement.notes: The selected source records concern cured epoxy binders. No reinforcing phase, fiber loading or composite classification is assigned; the resin mixture is not claimed to be a pure substance.

porosity.notes: No quantitative porosity of the selected tensile specimens is reported; zero porosity is not assumed.

orientation.notes: No specimen orientation relative to plate processing or molecular alignment is reported; no isotropy claim is made.

measured_tensile_strength.basis_note: Table 7 reports tensile strength for cured epoxy resins; section 2.5.1 describes tensile testing. The reported scalars are measured-source results, without a stated summary statistic or replicate count. They are not declared means, individual-specimen values, predictions, universal bounds or engineering allowables.

temperature.notes: Tensile-test temperature is not reported in the inspected method or Table 7. Cure and rheology temperatures do not establish it.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6, section 2.5.1

test_standard.notes: This is the source-reported standard citation, not independent compliance verification or a source for missing temperature, humidity, specimen count or statistics.

test_method.text: Tensile testing on a 50ST universal electromechanical testing machine (Tinius Olsen), using cured binder specimens milled from a 4 mm-thick plate.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6, section 2.5.1

test_method.notes: Only tensile strength is selected; no modulus extraction, engineering-versus-true stress convention or additional property is inferred.

direction.notes: Loading orientation relative to the plate or processing direction is not specified; isotropy is not inferred.

conditioning.notes: Tensile-specific conditioning, moisture, humidity and storage duration are not reported in the inspected passages.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6, section 2.5.1

loading_rate.notes: Preserve the source-reported stretching speed; it is not a strain rate in inverse seconds.

fact.notes: No tensile-test relative humidity is stated in the inspected passages.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6, section 2.5.1

fact.notes: Source plate thickness only; no per-specimen metrology or tolerance is inferred.

measured_tensile_strength.uncertainty_note: The inspected tensile method and Table 7 do not state specimen/replicate count, aggregation or central-statistic definition, uncertainty, standard deviation, standard error or confidence interval. A cited test standard does not supply these missing facts.

sample_count.scope: Specimen and independent replicate counts for the selected cured formulation tensile result are unknown.
sample_count.source_statement: The inspected tensile method and Table 7 do not state specimen/replicate count, aggregation or central-statistic definition, uncertainty, standard deviation, standard error or confidence interval. A cited test standard does not supply these missing facts.

method_definition.definition: Source-reported tensile testing under GOST 11262-2017 (ISO 527-2:2012), on a 50ST machine at a stretching speed of 10 mm/min, using specimens cut from a 4 mm-thick cured binder plate. No strain-extraction window is assigned to this tensile-strength record.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6, section 2.5.1

source_discrepancies.description: Table 1 labels the nominal feeds HCP:BPF:ECH as 1:8:16 through 1:24:16, while the listed reagent mole amounts and the section 2.2.1 statement about a constant 16-fold ECH excess do not establish a consistent normalized ratio.
source_discrepancies.disposition: Preserve the printed ratio labels as nominal source recipe labels. Do not recompute ECH amounts, repair the ratios, infer the intended denominator or claim validated feed stoichiometry or final composition.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4, section 2.2.1 opening paragraph and Table 1

source_discrepancies.description: Table 1 lists HCP as 35 (0.086) g (Mole) for PNA-BPF-2, but as 35 (0.101) for PNA-BPF-1 and PNA-BPF-S.
source_discrepancies.disposition: Keep the PNA-BPF-2 source label and its printed nominal 1:9:16 recipe without silently correcting the mass or mole entry. No recalculated composition is emitted.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4, Table 1, HCP g (Mole) column, PNA-BPF-2 versus PNA-BPF-1 and PNA-BPF-S

source_discrepancies.description: Section 2.1 names potassium hydroxide, whereas the synthesis headings, Table 1 and sections 2.2.1-2.2.2 describe NaOH or sodium hydroxide.
source_discrepancies.disposition: Retain the contradiction. The selected route is source-described batch addition of solid alkali; the alkali chemical identity is not independently resolved or silently changed from KOH to NaOH.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4, section 2.1 alkali entry, section 2.2.1 heading and Table 1; p.5, sections 2.2.1-2.2.2
